title: Selling Plans Seller Terms — Final Value Fees on Sold Orders
content:
**Terms in force.** When an order's payment is captured, the seller's **Selling Plans** plan on the order date bills final value fees on it. The variable component is the fee group rate (the item category mapped through the fee category map) on the fee basis up to the threshold, plus the above-threshold rate on any excess. The per-order component is the low fee when the fee basis is at or below the breakpoint and the high fee above it. The discount never touches the per-order fee or the surcharge. When the standing level on the order date is one of the surcharge standing levels, a separate below-standard surcharge component of the surcharge rate times the fee basis is billed. A seller can never be at a discount level and a surcharge level at once, so discount and surcharge never apply to the same order.

> **Retired clause — no longer in force.** "When the seller's performance standing level on the order date is one of the discount standing levels and the order shipped within the discount's maximum handling business days, the variable component is reduced by the discount rate." This clause of the final value fee terms is no longer in force and is superseded by the current basis.

## The components of a sold order's final value fees

| Component | When it is billed | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Variable final value fee | On every order whose payment is captured | The fee group rate times the fee basis up to the per-order threshold, plus the above-threshold rate times any part of the fee basis above the threshold, rounded to the nearest cent |
| Per-order fee | On every order whose payment is captured | The low per-order fee when the fee basis is at or below the breakpoint; the high per-order fee when it is above |
| Below-standard surcharge | Only when the seller's standing level on the order date is one of the surcharge standing levels | The surcharge rate times the fee basis, rounded to the nearest cent |

All rates, the threshold, the breakpoint and the fee category map are those of the plan held on the order date. Each component is a separate fee record for the order, billed on the order's capture date, showing the fee component, the fee group the item category maps to, whether the standing discount reduced the component and the fee basis (item subtotal plus shipping, tax excluded).

## Worked example (hypothetical order, Basic Store figures)

A seller on the Basic Store sells a home and kitchen item; the order's fee basis is USD 8000.00 and the seller is at Below Standard Level on the order date.

1. Fee group: home and kitchen maps to the most categories group, rate 12.7%.
2. Variable fee: 12.7% of the first USD 7500.00 is USD 952.50; the excess of USD 500.00 at 2.35% is USD 11.75; together USD 964.25.
3. Per-order fee: the fee basis is above the USD 10.00 breakpoint, so the high fee of USD 0.40 applies.
4. Below-standard surcharge: 6% of USD 8000.00 is USD 480.00, billed as its own component.

## Points of judgement

- **Category mapping.** The fee group comes from the order's item category through the plan's fee category map, never from the seller's description of the item.
- **Order date governs.** The plan held, and the standing level, are those on the order date.
- **Surcharge and per-order fee are separate.** The surcharge is a component of its own; it is not added into the variable fee.

superseded_clauses: When the seller's performance standing level on the order date is one of the discount standing levels and the order shipped within the discount's maximum handling business days, the variable component is reduced by the discount rate
